correctness.rationale: The Moore–Penrose Green kernel is reconstructed directly from the three orthogonal spectral subspaces of K_m square K_n. The finite transfer-current identity supplies each edge covariance and requires the common edge variance as a separate positive contribution. A complete mutually exclusive table of incident edge-pair currents gives the claimed rational cubic numerator. Descartes’ rule, exact values at m=2 and at consecutive integers n(n+1)/2-1 and n(n+1)/2, and the n=2 factorization prove all integer signs. An independent standard-library exact-rational checker compared the full transfer-current double sum to the rational formula for 2<=m,n<=12, tested thresholds, and independently enumerated small spanning trees; 313 assertions passed. Finite checks are not used as proof for unbounded m,n.

originality.rationale: The precise claim is a rational finite-parameter covariance with an integer-sign phase boundary at the triangular number m=n(n+1)/2 for ambient-adjacent vertex degrees of a uniform spanning tree on K_m square K_n. The Burton–Pemantle determinantal framework and Rapoport’s general degree-field formalism imply an algorithm for such covariances but do not supply this evaluated two-factor formula or exact sign phase diagram in inspected statements. Hladký–Nachmias–Tran provide one-root asymptotic results for dense graph sequences, not this sharp finite two-root boundary. Huh–Schröter–Wang establish edge-level negative correlations, which cannot settle the adjacent vertex-degree sign because of the shared edge. Rook-graph gonality is a different invariant. Other accessible research claims and indexed public mathematics records showed related but not implicationally stronger statements. Historical priority and possible unpublished rook-graph specializations remain risks.

value.rationale: The sharp triangular-number aspect-ratio boundary is a natural, all-parameter sign classification for the joint degrees of adjacent vertices on the rectangular rook graph. Edge indicators are negatively associated, so the positive region reveals the nontrivial competition between a shared-edge variance and negative cross-edge terms. The critical ratio m/n^2 -> 1/2 and its exact finite cutoff are structural features not obtained from a one-vertex local limit or an unevaluated general transfer-current determinant. The formula applies to every integer pair and can guide other product-graph correlation problems; no arbitrary fixed finite slice is used.
